entry.title: Research culture
entry.content:
I am lucky to have been part of a movement at Oxford to try and better the research culture that has provided me with a number of unique experiences while trying to speak up for others.

Most recently that takes the form of being a UK Research Staff Association representative on the Researcher Development Concordat Strategy Group led by Prof Richard Emes.

In a meeting recently I was reminded of the a Taoist principle that the best leader helps in an invisible way such that when the work is done people say they did it themselves. Tao Te Ching (Dao De Jing) Chapter 17 by Lao Tzu.

entry.title: Digital Gardening
entry.content:
A public space where notes grow, interlink, and are cultivated. Typically, the maturity of a note is shown through a borrowed nomenclature of seedlings through to evergreens.
The idea (from what I can find) was developed by Maggie Appleton and you can see a walkthrough of the journey in her History & Ethos page in her garden.

I see this as an opportunity not to have to produce a publication schedule or even coherently order the stuff I'm doing as the links rather than chronology does the work of building the garden.

Found useful resources from Wanderloots (including how to set this up) and the discussions in the Decapsulate podcast. All obviously helped by the fact I have been using obsidian for years and love a productivity push.

entry.title: Decapsulate
entry.content:
A podcast by Tris and Robin

Last I looked there are only 7 episodes and I listened to them all over a couple of days.

Reminded me a bit of the early years of Cortex without the podcasting machine that is Myke Hurley falling into interviewer mode. Also because of the RSI chat from Tris being reminiscent of CGP Grey's troubles.

That being said the two key things I took from it are the ideas of Digital Gardening and Techno-Feudalism.
